An organization chart showing the structure of financial institutions in Nigeria. At the very top is the "Central Bank of Nigeria (Apex Regulator)". Below it, arrows point down to "Commercial Banks", "Merchant Banks", "Mortgage Banks", and "Development Banks". To the side, independent but related, is a box for "Insurance Companies" regulated by NAICOM, and a box for "Traditional Institutions (Esusu/Ajo)" with no formal regulator line. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A flowchart showing the money creation process. A person (Depositor 1) hands ₦10,000 cash to "Bank A". An arrow splits from Bank A: ₦2,000 goes to a vault ("Reserve 20%"), and an arrow showing ₦8,000 goes to "Borrower 1". Borrower 1 gives the money to "Merchant", who deposits ₦8,000 into "Bank B". An arrow splits from Bank B: ₦1,600 goes to a vault, and ₦6,400 goes to "Borrower 2". A box at the bottom states: "Total deposits eventually equal ₦50,000".
